newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Record Australia domestic air activity in Oct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Record Australia domestic air activity in Oct.

text.p: Australian airlines carried 2.28 million revenue passengers in October last year, up 3.9 percent over the previous month, the Department of Transport and Regional Development said on Thursday.

"October 1996 continued the upward trend in domestic airline activity with total revenue passengers, revenue passenger kilometres and available seat kilometres all recording new industry highs," the department said in a statement.
Revenue passengers carried in October rose 4.6 percent from a year earlier while total revenue passenger kilometres jumped 5.4 percent over the year earlier level.
The department said available seat capacity increased 7.6 percent in October over October 1995 to the highest seat availability on record.
"On an individual city pair basis, all but two of the top 20 routes recorded increased passenger levels in October 1996," it said.
The most significant increase was on the Brisbane to Townsville route, which recorded a rise of 11.6 percent.
The number of passengers on the Brisbane to Melbourne route rose 10.0 percent, while Coolangatta to Melbourne increased 9.6 percent and Launceston to Melbourne jumped 9.2 percent.
Total revenue passenger load factors averaged 73.1 percent during October 1996, compared to 74.6 percent in October 1995.
